anya: Heads-up — ran the full onboarding eval for cedar-embed (int6 per-channel) against our short-query and wiki100k suites, and we have a weird norm shift + recall hit. Posting quick numbers and next steps.

sam: numbers?

anya: baseline (float32) vs int6-pch: recall@1 0.748 -> 0.703 (-4.5%), recall@5 0.902 -> 0.891 (-1.2%), pairwise AUC 0.912 -> 0.887, cluster purity (kmeans k=100) 0.64 -> 0.61. Also saw mean L2 norm drop: 21.7 -> 17.9 and variance tightened.

jordan: that norm change smells like quantization scale mismatch or bias folding. Did you check per-layer scales and zero-point drift?

anya: yep. Per-layer scales look sane on weights, but the final projection layer activations have a reduced dynamic range after quant. Quick inspect output distribution: 
```
# last-proj activations (sample)
float32: mean=0.0123 std=0.287 max=2.13 min=-1.98
int6-pch: mean=0.0091 std=0.238 max=1.76 min=-1.64
```
Suggests clipping/rounding reducing magnitude -> embeddings shrink.

tess: can we try spherical normalization post-embed? i.e., L2 normalize before recall. if norm collapse is main driver it might recover recall.

anya: ran a quick ablation: +L2 norming (on both index and queries) restored recall@1 to 0.733 (half the gap) and recall@5 to 0.898. Still short of float32 but much better. Also tried temperature scaling on cosine (temp=0.08) — small lift.

sam: what about re-scaling with learned per-dim gain (small linear layer after embed) — cheap retrain?

anya: I tried a tiny calibration step: fit diag-scaling (per-dim multiplicative) on 10k pairs (MSE to float embeddings). That recovered recall@1 to 0.742, recall@5 0.903 (basically matched baseline). So calibration + norming seems promising.

jordan: nice. Did you compare per-tensor int6 vs per-channel?

anya: yes — per-tensor int6 had worse recall (recall@1 ~0.683) and larger norm collapse. Per-channel looks more stable but still needs calibration.

tess: can you push the eval config and calibration script? I'll open a tiny PR to add calibration step to the onboard pipeline and mark as optional. Also we should add a metric: mean embedding norm delta (abs) to detect this early.

anya: done — uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/cedar/1766009999/{metrics.csv,calib_diag.npy,calib_script.py,config.yaml}. Quick eval command I ran:
```
embed-validate --model cedar-embed --quant int6-pch --datasets shortq,wiki100k --metrics recall@1,5,auc,centroid-mmd,norm-delta --calib s3://redwood-evals/cedar/1766009999/calib_diag.npy
```

eval-bot: nightly-eval finished for cedar-embed (int6-pch) — status: FAIL (regression >3% recall@1). See s3 artifacts.

sam: ok plan: 1) add norm-delta alert in pipeline (tess) 2) add optional calib step to onboard (tess + anya) 3) run lightweight floating calibration (10k pairs) in PR 4) rerun full wiki100k suite and report. Can we also include cosine vs L2 experiments in the run?

anya: yes will include both distances and a small uMAP snapshot export. Putting a note in PR with numbers and suggested default: enable diag-calib by default for int6-pch, and L2-normalize at recall time as cheap fallback.

jordan: thanks — if PR lands I'll queue a canary rollout to staging index to sanity-check latency impact. :eyes:
